summary: Profiled the search hot path by node census, built a semantics-preserving optimised engine, leaf and search achieving a 3.08x end-to-end speedup behind bit-exactness gates, and established that measured work is an order of magnitude below the worst-case bound the programme had been using for scheduling.
validationPerformed: Leaf bit-exactness over 225,183 real leaf states, 0 bit-pattern mismatches; wave and readiness tables exact against their transcendental originals.
Trajectory gate over 8,288 games, 438,020 moves and 548,263 waves, 0 mismatches; search parity over 306 moves across nine configurations with 0 action, work or completed-depth mismatches.
Speedups measured by interleaved A/B at steady load after a drifting-load artifact was identified and discarded.
limitations: Recorded by the coordinator on the delegated agent's behalf; the agent had no write access to research/ and did not review this transcription.
Exploratory namespace only; does not upgrade docs/research/ or any frozen protocol.
The optimised engine is a parallel implementation; no existing engine, search or reference source was modified and nothing outside its own directory uses it.
Optimisations that would have changed floating-point results, logical work counts or cache semantics were rejected and are listed rather than adopted.
